introduction: Parley serves each workspace's repository over git smart HTTP at its own address, authenticating clients with hub credentials, applying the hub's access rules, deciding each ref of a push before any of it reaches the store, and protecting the namespace the hub keeps for itself.

glossary.pkt-line error: A refusal expressed in git's wire framing, so that the git client shows the message to the person rather than failing without explanation.
glossary.protected namespace: refs/hub/replaced/, which the hub maintains and no client push may create, update or delete, on any workspace and with any credential.
glossary.push control: The decision Parley makes about each update of a registered patch branch — refuse it, forward it to the fork first, accept and mirror it, or simply accept it — taken from the patch_branch_source and push_patches_to_origin settings.
glossary.registered patch branch: A refs/heads/<name> on a carry_patch workspace whose <name> is a patch of that workspace that is not deleted and is not the integration branch.
glossary.relay: Passing a client's git request through to the repository store with a store token Parley mints for the purpose and never discloses.

requirements.title: Where a repository is served
requirements.rationale: hub_url is what a client clones, so the address the service reports and the address it serves have to be the same one.

criteria.action: serve each workspace's repository at the external URL followed by /git/<org-slug>/<workspace-slug>.git
criteria.contract: a git client cloning that URL with a valid credential receives the repository; the path is built from the workspace's organization slug and its own slug

criteria.condition: a git request names a path without the .git suffix, or names a workspace whose organization does not match the path
criteria.action: answer that the repository was not found
criteria.contract: a pkt-line 404 "ERR repository not found"; the two cases are indistinguishable

criteria.action: report in a workspace's hub_url exactly the address this service serves, and null when the workspace has no organization or the service has no external URL
criteria.contract: cloning the non-null hub_url of a ready workspace succeeds; a workspace with no organization reports null and is served at no git URL

requirements.title: Authenticating a git client
requirements.rationale: git speaks Basic auth, and a refusal it cannot render is a user staring at a failure with no reason.

criteria.action: accept the HTTP Basic password as a hub credential — an API key, a personal access token or an admin token — and ignore the username
criteria.contract: the same credential works whatever username accompanies it; each of the three kinds is accepted on a route its access allows

criteria.condition: a git request carries no credential, an unacceptable one, or one whose user is blocked
criteria.action: refuse it
criteria.contract: HTTP 401 with a pkt-line error; the refusal does not say which of the three conditions applied

criteria.action: express every refusal of a git request in git's pkt-line framing
criteria.contract: for each refusal the git client prints the message to the person; the body is well-formed pkt-line and not a JSON envelope

criteria.action: never accept a repository store token from a client and never disclose one to a client
criteria.contract: a store token offered as the Basic password is refused like any unknown credential; no response body or header carries a store token

requirements.title: Who may fetch and who may push
requirements.rationale: This is the access decision of package 03 applied where a mistake hands out or destroys code rather than returning a wrong JSON field.

criteria.action: serve a fetch and a push to the workspace's owner and to an admin token, and serve a fetch to a member of the workspace's organization with the owner's result
criteria.contract: the owner, an admin token and a member all receive the same pack for the same fetch; the owner and the admin token may also push

criteria.condition: a member of the workspace's organization attempts a push, or the ref advertisement for the receive service
criteria.action: refuse it as a member
criteria.contract: a pkt-line 403 "ERR org members have read-only access to this workspace"; the repository is unchanged

criteria.condition: a caller with no access to the workspace, or a token bound to another workspace, makes any git request
criteria.action: answer that the repository was not found, for a fetch and a push alike
criteria.contract: a pkt-line 404 "ERR repository not found"; the answer is identical for a workspace that exists, one that does not, and one the caller may not see

criteria.action: check the workspace and its organization against the URL, then that its repository is ready, then access, then a personal access token's git scope, in that order
criteria.contract: a member's push is refused as a member whatever the PAT's scopes; a workspace whose repository is not ready answers "ERR repository not available" before access is considered

criteria.condition: the access lookup for a git request fails
criteria.action: refuse the request rather than granting any level
criteria.contract: a pkt-line 500 internal server error; no pack is served and no ref is updated

criteria.condition: a personal access token lacks the git scope the request needs
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: a pkt-line 403; git:read is needed to fetch and git:write to push, and git:write grants git:read

requirements.title: Fetching
requirements.rationale: A clone that transfers the whole history on every fetch is a cost the store charges for, and an advertisement git cannot parse is a clone that never starts.

criteria.condition: the ref advertisement is requested with a valid service
criteria.action: answer with git's advertisement for that service
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with Content-Type application/x-<service>-advertisement and a body a git client accepts

criteria.condition: the ref advertisement is requested with a missing or invalid service parameter
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: a pkt-line 403 "ERR invalid or missing service parameter"

criteria.condition: a client fetches into a repository that already holds part of the history
criteria.action: transfer only the objects the client lacks
criteria.contract: the bytes transferred for a fetch after one new commit are a small fraction of a full clone's, and the client ends with the same refs either way

criteria.action: serve whichever protocol version the client asks for among those the store speaks, and accept a gzip-encoded request body
criteria.contract: a client asking for protocol v2 and one asking for v0 both clone successfully, and a request with Content-Encoding gzip is served

requirements.title: Pushing
requirements.rationale: The per-ref report is how a client learns what happened, and a push that reports success for a ref it did not apply is a lost commit.

criteria.condition: a caller with write access pushes refs the service accepts
criteria.action: apply them to the workspace's repository and answer with git's per-ref report
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with Content-Type application/x-git-receive-pack-result; each accepted ref is reported ok and is readable at its new value afterwards

criteria.action: report the outcome of every ref of a push, and apply exactly the refs it reported as accepted
criteria.contract: for any push, the set of refs whose value changed equals the set reported ok

criteria.condition: a push is refused before any ref is applied
criteria.action: leave the repository unchanged
criteria.contract: every ref holds the value it held before the push

requirements.title: Push control on a carry-patch workspace
requirements.rationale: The store offers no pre-receive hook, so the four documented outcomes have to be produced in front of it, per ref, without disturbing the rest of the push.

criteria.condition: a carry_patch workspace has patch_branch_source origin and push_patches_to_origin false
criteria.action: refuse an update of a registered patch branch, telling the client where to push instead
criteria.contract: the ref is reported ng with "branch is synced from origin; push to <git_url> instead", or "branch is synced from origin; delete it on the fork instead" for a deletion; the git_url carries no userinfo and the ref keeps its old value

criteria.condition: a carry_patch workspace has patch_branch_source origin and push_patches_to_origin true
criteria.action: push the update to the fork first, without forcing, and accept it only if the fork accepts it
criteria.contract: on the fork's acceptance the ref is reported ok and holds the new value; on its refusal the ref is reported ng with "origin rejected push: <error>" and keeps its old value; a deletion is refused as under the previous setting

criteria.condition: a carry_patch workspace has patch_branch_source hub and push_patches_to_origin true
criteria.action: accept the update and then force-push it to the fork on a best-effort basis
criteria.contract: the ref is reported ok and holds the new value whether or not the mirror succeeded; a failed mirror does not fail the push

criteria.condition: a carry_patch workspace has patch_branch_source hub and push_patches_to_origin false, or the workspace is standard, or the ref is not a registered patch branch
criteria.action: accept the update under the ordinary access rules, applying no push control
criteria.contract: the ref is reported ok and holds the new value; no request is made to the fork

criteria.action: decide push control for each ref of a push on its own
criteria.contract: in a push carrying a refused patch branch and an ordinary branch, the ordinary branch is applied and reported ok while the patch branch is reported ng

requirements.title: The protected namespace
requirements.rationale: The hub keeps replaced patch tips there, and a client that can overwrite them can destroy the only copy of work it replaced.

criteria.condition: a client push creates, updates or deletes a ref under refs/hub/replaced/
criteria.action: refuse that ref while processing the rest of the push
criteria.contract: the push reports unpack ok; the ref is reported "ng <ref> refs/hub/replaced/ is maintained by the hub and cannot be pushed to"; the ref keeps its old value or stays absent

criteria.action: apply the protection on every workspace and for every credential, the owner and an admin token included
criteria.contract: the same refusal is produced for a standard and a carry_patch workspace, and for an API key, a PAT and an admin token alike

criteria.condition: the repository store accepts refs outside refs/heads/ and refs/tags/
criteria.action: serve those refs to a fetch as any other ref
criteria.contract: git ls-remote lists them and a fetch of refs/hub/replaced/<branch> retrieves it; where the store does not accept the namespace, the read is unavailable and the push refusal above still holds

requirements.title: After a push
requirements.rationale: head_sha is what every client reads to know where the workspace stands, and a stale one makes the whole record untrustworthy.

criteria.condition: a push completes, whatever its outcome
criteria.action: refresh the workspace's head_sha from the repository's HEAD
criteria.contract: head_sha matches the repository's HEAD afterwards, including after a push whose every ref was refused

criteria.action: let only the refs a push accepted have any effect beyond the head_sha refresh
criteria.contract: a refused ref triggers no forward, no mirror and no change to the workspace record other than head_sha

execution_paths.title: An agent clones the workspace and pushes a branch back

steps.action: clones the workspace's hub_url, offering the user's API key as the Basic password
authenticates the credential, admits the owner, mints a read token for the workspace's repository and relays the advertisement and the pack
serves the objects for the relayed fetch
commits and pushes a new branch
decides each ref, relays the accepted push to the store and reports ok for the branch
refreshes the workspace's head_sha from the repository's HEAD

execution_paths.title: A member clones the repository and is refused a push

steps.action: clones the workspace's hub_url with their own credential
admits the member for the fetch and serves the same pack the owner would receive
refuses with the pkt-line 403 for a member, before the PAT's scopes are considered
receives nothing, and the repository is unchanged

execution_paths.title: A patch branch is refused while the rest of the same push lands

steps.action: pushes two refs at once to a carry_patch workspace whose patch branches come from the fork: a registered patch branch and an ordinary branch
reads the push's ref commands before relaying anything and applies push control to each
relays only the ordinary branch to the store and merges its report with the refusal of the patch branch
sees the ordinary branch reported ok and the patch branch reported ng with the message naming where to push instead

execution_paths.title: A push to the protected namespace is rejected per ref

steps.action: pushes an update to refs/hub/replaced/<branch> together with an ordinary branch, as the workspace's owner
reports unpack ok, refuses the protected ref with the fixed message and relays the ordinary branch
applies the ordinary branch and leaves the protected ref untouched
sees one ref ok and one ng, and the protected ref still holds its old value
